questions.q: What is the weak-to-strong generalization experimental setup designed to be an analogy for?
options: Comparing the energy efficiency of small versus large models
The future situation where humans must supervise AI systems more capable than themselves, studied today by having a genuinely weaker model supervise a genuinely stronger one
Deciding which model architecture trains fastest on limited hardware
Testing whether small models can be deployed more cheaply than large ones
questions.explain: The setup deliberately swaps in a weak model for a human supervisor and a strong model for a superhuman model, as a tractable stand-in researchers can study now.

questions.q: What was the headline empirical finding of the weak-to-strong generalization paper?
options: The strong model always perfectly copied every mistake the weak supervisor made
A strong model fine-tuned only on a weak supervisor's labels substantially outperformed that weak supervisor on several tested tasks, rather than just imitating its errors
Weak supervisors consistently outperformed the strong models they were training
No measurable generalization occurred under any tested condition
questions.explain: The strong model generalized beyond the weak labels' mistakes in several settings, which was not guaranteed given that weak labels were its only training signal.

questions.q: What is the important caveat sitting next to that headline result?
options: The experiment could not be run on any NLP tasks at all
Naive fine-tuning on weak labels recovered only part of the strong model's full capability, leaving a meaningful gap unclosed
The strong model's performance was identical to the weak supervisor's in every single case
The result only applies to image classification, not language tasks
questions.explain: Naive fine-tuning closed only part of the gap between weak-supervisor performance and the strong model's full ground-truth-supervised capability, which is the risk this testbed is meant to flag.

questions.q: What does the auxiliary confidence loss do?
options: It forces the strong model to match the weak label exactly in every case
It explicitly allows the strong model to disagree with a weak label when the strong model is confident in a different answer, which improved recovered performance
It removes the weak supervisor from the training process entirely
It reduces the total amount of training data required to zero
questions.explain: The auxiliary confidence loss lets genuine strong-model knowledge win out over a known-flawed weak label in a principled way, rather than forcing exact agreement.

questions.q: Why do the paper's authors describe this setup as an analogy rather than a direct simulation of superhuman oversight?
options: Because current strong models are not superhuman in any deep sense, and a weak model's mistakes may not resemble the mistakes a human overseer would make with a genuinely superhuman model
Because the experiment was never actually run on real models
Because analogy and simulation mean the exact same thing in this context
Because the researchers consider the future oversight problem already fully solved
questions.explain: The setup studies the dynamics of weak-supervising-strong today as a tractable stand-in, since the real future problem of humans supervising superhuman systems doesn't yet exist to experiment on directly.
